passage:
My best friend is Amy. We have known each other since childhood. We live in the same neighbourhood and go to the same school.

Amy is kind and helpful. When I feel sad, she listens to me carefully. When I have problems with my homework, she helps me. Last week, I lost my wallet at the market. Amy gave me some money for the bus.

We seldom quarrel. If we do, we forgive each other quickly. True friends share happy times and support each other in difficult times. I am lucky to have Amy as my best friend.
q: Who is the writer's best friend?
explain: 原文首句：My best friend is Amy.

passage:
Last summer, my family took a trip to London. We flew from Guangzhou to London. The flight took eleven hours.

We stayed in London for a week. We visited the British Museum and saw many old Chinese treasures. We took photos in front of Big Ben. We rode on the London Eye and enjoyed the beautiful view of the city.

London food is interesting. I liked the fish and chips very much, but I missed Chinese rice. The weather was cool even in summer, so I wore a jacket every day.

It was my first trip abroad. I learned a lot about British culture. I hope to visit more countries in the future.
q: Where did the writer's family go last summer?
explain: 原文：my family took a trip to London.

passage:
Three years ago, we found a small dog on the street. He was wet, cold and hungry. My dad carried him home. We called him Lucky.

Lucky is very clever. He can shake hands, sit and even open the door. He waits by the window every afternoon when I come home from school. He is my loyal friend.

Last year, Lucky saved my little brother. My brother ran to the street to catch a ball. A car came fast. Lucky ran after him and pushed him back. The car missed them both!

Animals have feelings. They can be our true friends if we show them kindness.
q: When did the family find the dog?
explain: 原文：Three years ago, we found a small dog on the street.

passage:
Trees are the oldest and tallest living things on Earth. Some trees can live for thousands of years.

Trees are very important to us. They give us oxygen and clean the air. They also give shade in summer and keep the soil safe with their long roots. Without trees, strong rain can wash away the land and deserts grow bigger.

Many animals and birds live on trees. Monkeys jump between branches. Birds build nests in the leaves. A forest without trees is like a city without people.

Sadly, humans cut down many trees every day. We need wood for paper, chairs and houses. But if we keep cutting, one day there will be no forests left.
q: What do trees give us?
explain: 原文：They give us oxygen and clean the air.

passage:
It was Sunday morning. I turned on the tap to brush my teeth, but no water came out! I ran to the kitchen — the same! My mum said, "The water pipes are being repaired today. We will have no water until the evening."

What a day! I couldn't wash my face or flush the toilet. I used a small bottle of water to brush my teeth. At lunchtime, Mum bought some noodles from a restaurant because we couldn't cook at home.

In the afternoon, I was very thirsty. I went to the shop and bought a big bottle of water. It cost 5 yuan. I drank it slowly.

When the water came back at 8 p.m., I was so happy. I filled a glass and drank carefully. I finally understood: every drop of water is precious.
q: What day was it in the story?
explain: 原文：It was Sunday morning.

passage:
Last Friday evening, there was a big storm. Suddenly, all the lights went out. My family was having dinner in the dark. Dad found some candles and lit them one by one.

Without electricity, everything stopped. The TV was off. The fridge was warm. My computer game was gone. I couldn't even charge my phone. But we had a lovely dinner by candlelight. Mum told old stories and Dad sang songs from his childhood.

The power came back at midnight. Suddenly the room was bright again. I turned on my phone and saw many messages from my friends — they were in the dark too.

That night, I learned how much our modern life needs electricity. And I also learned that family time is more important than any screen.
q: What happened last Friday evening?
options: A big storm came and the lights went out
explain: 原文：there was a big storm. Suddenly, all the lights went out.

passage:
I love reading poems. A good poem is like a song — short, beautiful, and full of feeling.

My favourite poem is Quiet Night Thoughts by Li Bai. It has only four short lines, but it touches every Chinese heart. It says: in the quiet night, the moonlight on the floor looks like frost. The poet looks up at the moon and then down, missing his home far away.

I like this poem because it is simple but deep. When I am far from home at summer camp, I remember these lines. The moon looks the same in every city, so I know my family is with me under the same moon.

Poems are small, but they carry big dreams. Try writing one of your own!
q: What is the writer's favourite poem?
options: Quiet Night Thoughts by Li Bai
explain: 原文：My favourite poem is Quiet Night Thoughts by Li Bai.

passage:
Chef Liu is a famous cook in Guangzhou. But twenty years ago, cooking was just his hobby.

When he was a boy, he loved watching his grandmother cook. He tried his first fried egg at the age of eight. He burned it, but he kept trying. Every weekend, he cooked for his family. His friends loved eating at his house.

After high school, he went to a cooking school. It was hard work — he practised every day from early morning to late night. Ten years later, he opened his own small restaurant. Now his restaurant is in a five-star hotel, and he teaches young cooks on TV.

"Start from what you love," Chef Liu says. "A hobby today can be your career tomorrow. But remember — you need passion and practice every single day."
q: What is Chef Liu famous for?
explain: 原文：Chef Liu is a famous cook in Guangzhou.

When he was a boy, he loved watching his grandmother cook. He tried his first fried egg at the age of eight. He burned it, but he kept trying. Every weekend, he cooked for his family. His friends loved eating at his house.

After high school, he went to a cooking school. It was hard work — he practised every day from early morning to late night. Ten years later, he opened his own small restaurant. Now his restaurant is in a five-star hotel, and he teaches young cooks on TV.

"Start from what you love," Chef Liu says. "A hobby today can be your career tomorrow. But remember — you need passion and practice every single day."
q: What was cooking to him twenty years ago?
explain: 原文：twenty years ago, cooking was just his hobby.
